memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"The LORD said to Moses, 'Consecrate to me every firstborn male. The first
offspring of every womb among the Israelites belongs to me, whether human or
animal.'" - Ex 13:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The night is barely over. The dust of Egypt is still on their feet. And the
first instruction God gives His newly freed people is about the firstborn.

The reason is written into what just happened. Every Israelite firstborn son was
alive that morning only because a lamb had died in his place. God is saying:
these lives are Mine by right. I bought them.

Notice the word "consecrate." It means to set apart for God. Not to destroy, but
to dedicate. The firstborn son was not sacrificed; he was marked as belonging to
God, and later verses will explain how he was redeemed.

This is the logic of the whole Bible. Because you were rescued, you belong. Paul
puts it plainly: "You are not your own; you were bought at a price. Therefore
honor God with your bodies" (1 Cor 6:19-20).

Notice also that God asks for the first, not the leftovers. The first of the
womb, and elsewhere the first of the harvest. What we give first reveals what we
value most. If God gets what remains after everything else has been spent, He
has not really been given anything.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Does God receive the first of your time and money, or the leftovers?
2. What would it look like to live today as someone who belongs to God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, You bought me at great cost and I belong to You. Help me to give You the
first and best, not what is left over. Amen.
